struct.title: X-ray crystallographic structure of a beta-hairpin peptide derived from Abeta 17-36. (ORN)LVFFAED(ORN)AII(N-Me-Gly)LMV

pubmed.rcsb_pubmed_abstract_text: Amyloid-β (Aβ) forms heterogeneous oligomers, which are implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Many Aβ oligomers consist of β-hairpin building blocks─Aβ peptides in β-hairpin conformations. β-Hairpins of Aβ can adopt a variety of alignments, but the role that β-hairpin alignment plays in the formation and heterogeneity of Aβ oligomers is poorly understood. To explore the effect of β-hairpin alignment on the oligomerization of Aβ peptides, we designed and studied two model peptides with two different β-hairpin alignments. Peptides Aβm <sub>17-36 </sub> and Aβm <sub>17-35 </sub> mimic two different β-hairpins that Aβ can form, the Aβ <sub>17-36 </sub> and Aβ <sub>17-35 </sub> β-hairpins, respectively. These hairpins are similar in composition but differ in hairpin alignment, altering the facial arrangements of the side chains of the residues that they contain. X-ray crystallography and SDS-PAGE demonstrate that the difference in facial arrangement between these peptides leads to distinct oligomer formation. In the crystal state, Aβm <sub>17-36 </sub> forms triangular trimers that further assemble to form hexamers, while Aβm <sub>17-35 </sub> forms tetrameric β-barrels. In SDS-PAGE, Aβm <sub>17-36 </sub> assembles to form a ladder of oligomers, while Aβm <sub>17-35 </sub> either assembles to form a dimer or does not assemble at all. The differences in the behavior of Aβm <sub>17-36 </sub> and Aβm <sub>17-35 </sub> suggest β-hairpin alignment as a source of the observed heterogeneity of Aβ oligomers.
